plugin.sha1.title: SHA-1
plugin.sha1.preset.sha1-two-block: SHA-1 of the 56-byte example message (two blocks)
plugin.sha1.preset.sha1-empty: SHA-1 of the empty message (padding only)
plugin.sha1.param.encodingHint: Text is hashed as its UTF-8 bytes. Hex lets you enter any bytes, two hex digits per byte.
plugin.sha1.param.inputHint: 0 to 320 bytes, which pad to at most six 64-byte blocks. The message may be empty.
plugin.sha1.param.detailHint: “Per round” shows every message schedule word and every one of the 80 rounds. “Per block” runs the whole compression function of a block in one step.
plugin.sha1.op.pad: Pad the message to whole blocks
plugin.sha1.op.init: Load the chaining value and the block
plugin.sha1.op.compress: Run all rounds of the block
plugin.sha1.op.feedForward: Add the working variables to H (feed-forward)
plugin.sha1.step.initial: SHA-1 turns the {{bytes}}-byte message into a {{bits}}-bit hash value. It pads the message to whole {{blockBits}}-bit blocks, then runs the compression function ({{rounds}} rounds) once per block, starting from the initial hash value H(0).
plugin.sha1.step.pad_one: Padding (FIPS 180-4 §5.1.1, as for SHA-256): after the {{bytes}} message bytes ({{bits}} bits) come the byte 80 (the bit 1 and seven zero bits), {{zeros}} zero bytes and the message length in bits as a {{lengthBits}}-bit number, big-endian. The result is {{count}} block of {{blockBytes}} bytes.
plugin.sha1.step.pad_other: Padding (FIPS 180-4 §5.1.1, as for SHA-256): after the {{bytes}} message bytes ({{bits}} bits) come the byte 80 (the bit 1 and seven zero bits), {{zeros}} zero bytes and the message length in bits as a {{lengthBits}}-bit number, big-endian. The result is {{count}} blocks of {{blockBytes}} bytes.
plugin.sha1.step.initFirst: H(0) is the SHA-1 initial hash value (FIPS 180-4 §5.3.1): {{h}}. The working variables a … e start as H(0), and W₀ … W₁₅ are the 16 words of block 1, read big-endian.
plugin.sha1.step.init: Block {{n}} starts from the chaining value H({{prev}}) = {{h}}: a … e ← H({{prev}}), and W₀ … W₁₅ are the 16 words of block {{n}}. W₁₆ … W₇₉ still hold the words of block {{prev}} until the message schedule of block {{n}} overwrites them.
plugin.sha1.step.schedule: W{{t}} = ROTL¹(W{{t3}} ⊕ W{{t8}} ⊕ W{{t14}} ⊕ W{{t16}}): {{w3}} ⊕ {{w8}} ⊕ {{w14}} ⊕ {{w16}} = {{xor}}, rotated left by one bit: {{w}}. The one-bit rotation was added in 1995; the original SHA (now called SHA-0) lacked it.
plugin.sha1.step.round: Round {{t}}: T = ROTL⁵(a) + f{{t}}(b, c, d) + e + K{{t}} + W{{t}} = {{rotl5}} + {{f}} + {{e}} + {{k}} + {{w}} = {{T}} (mod 2^32), with f{{t}} = {{fn}}. Then e ← d, d ← c, c ← ROTL³⁰(b) = {{c}}, b ← a and a ← T.
plugin.sha1.step.compress: Block {{n}}: the message schedule and all {{rounds}} rounds in one step. Afterwards a … e = {{vars}}.
plugin.sha1.step.feedForward: Feed-forward: H({{n}}) = H({{prev}}) + (a, …, e), word by word mod 2^32 = {{h}}. Adding the input back makes the compression function hard to invert.
plugin.sha1.step.output: The SHA-1 hash value is the final chaining value H({{n}}) itself, all {{bits}} bits: {{digest}}.
plugin.sha1.formula.init: a … e ← H({{prev}}); W₀ … W₁₅ ← M({{n}})
plugin.sha1.formula.round: T = ROTL⁵(a) + {{fn}}(b, c, d) + e + K{{t}} + W{{t}}; e ← d; d ← c; c ← ROTL³⁰(b); b ← a; a ← T
plugin.sha1.error.encoding: Unknown input format “{{encoding}}”: choose text or hex.
plugin.sha1.error.inputLength: The message has {{length}} bytes; at most 320 bytes are allowed.
